title: ADA: A1c goal for many adults
summary: An A1c below 7% suits many nonpregnant adults when significant hypoglycemia is absent.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: Individualize the goal; do not convert this reference into an automatic treatment target.

title: Glycemic assessment interval
summary: Assess glycemia at least twice yearly; consider every three months after treatment changes or when goals are unmet.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: Review A1c reliability and clinical context.

title: Individualize glycemic goals
summary: A lower goal, such as <6.5%, may suit low treatment risk; frailty or substantial treatment harms may justify less stringent goals.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: This prototype does not calculate an individualized A1c goal.

title: VA/DoD: individualized A1c range
summary: VA/DoD suggests 7.0–8.5% for most adults with type 2 diabetes when safely achievable, individualized for complications, comorbidities and life expectancy.
evidenceNote: Original VA/DoD strength retained; separate evidence certainty not extracted.
cautions: Table 2 supplies more specific ranges; veteran status alone does not select an A1c target.
ADA and VA/DoD targets are presented separately.

title: Older adults: health-based A1c goals
summary: Consider <7.0–7.5% with stable health and intact function; <8.0% may suit complex health. With very poor health, prioritize avoiding hypoglycemia and symptomatic hyperglycemia.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: A birthday alone does not determine the goal.

title: Older adults with diabetes: BP goals
summary: Aim for <130/80 mmHg when safe (A); a relaxed goal, such as <140/90, may suit poor health, limited life expectancy or treatment harms (E).
evidenceNote: Grade A applies to the usual goal; E applies to the relaxed-goal option. No single combined grade is inferred.
cautions: Draft reference; verify the full recommendation before applying it.

title: Diabetes: annual kidney screening
summary: Check UACR and eGFR at least annually in all type 2 diabetes and in type 1 diabetes of ≥5 years’ duration.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: Albuminuria and eGFR are separate measurements.

title: Established CKD: monitoring frequency
summary: In established CKD, monitor UACR and eGFR 1–4 times yearly according to stage.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: Use the stage-specific figure and clinical circumstances to choose an interval.

title: Retinopathy screening intervals
summary: Start a comprehensive dilated exam at type 2 diagnosis or five years after type 1 onset. If prior annual exams are normal and glycemia is at goal, consider 1–2-year intervals.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: Existing retinopathy requires at least annual, and sometimes more frequent, eye assessment.

title: Comprehensive foot examination
summary: Perform a comprehensive foot evaluation at least annually. Inspect at every visit with sensory loss, previous ulceration or amputation.
evidenceNote: ADA evidence grades are retained in the strength field; they are not ACC/AHA classes or levels.
cautions: This reference does not replace an examination or determine wound urgency.

title: ADA: BP treatment goals in diabetes
summary: When safe, target <130/80 mmHg; encourage systolic BP <120 in people with high cardiovascular or kidney risk.
evidenceNote: Grade A applies to recommendation 10.4; individualization in recommendation 10.3 is grade B.
cautions: Individualize for adverse effects and preferences.

title: VA/DoD: who to test for CKD
summary: Consider UACR and eGFR testing with age >60, diabetes, hypertension, or cardiovascular disease, including heart failure.
evidenceNote: Original VA/DoD strength retained; separate evidence certainty not extracted.
cautions: Draft reference; verify the full recommendation before applying it.

title: VA/DoD: finerenone eligibility
summary: Consider finerenone on maximally tolerated ACEi/ARB with type 2 diabetes, UACR >30 mg/g, eGFR ≥25 mL/min/1.73 m² and potassium <4.8 mEq/L.
evidenceNote: Original VA/DoD strength retained; separate evidence certainty not extracted.
cautions: Guideline eligibility and VA formulary approval are separate checks.

title: VA/DoD: GLP-1 therapy in CKD
summary: Add a GLP-1 receptor agonist to ACEi/ARB therapy in type 2 diabetes with albuminuric CKD to improve kidney and cardiovascular outcomes.
evidenceNote: Original VA/DoD strength retained; separate evidence certainty not extracted.
cautions: Confirm the agent’s evidence, labeling and VA Criteria for Use.

title: CKD: SGLT2 indication
summary: Use an SGLT2 inhibitor with type 2 diabetes, CKD and eGFR ≥20; also in CKD with eGFR ≥20 plus UACR ≥200 mg/g, or heart failure regardless of albuminuria.
cautions: Verify full eligibility and product labeling.

title: Nephrology referral thresholds
summary: A five-year kidney-failure risk of 3–5% can support referral. Other criteria include eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² or persistent UACR >700 mg/g.
cautions: Selected criteria; verify the full referral figure and risk-model eligibility.

title: KDIGO: standardized systolic BP goal
summary: For high BP with nondialysis CKD, consider systolic BP <120 mmHg when tolerated, using standardized office measurement.
population: Adults with high BP and CKD.
evidenceNote: Original KDIGO 2B retained; not an ACC/AHA evidence level.
cautions: Do not apply this target to nonstandardized readings.
Limited life expectancy or symptomatic postural hypotension may justify less intensive therapy.

title: Albuminuric diabetic CKD: ACEi or ARB
summary: Start an ACE inhibitor or ARB for high BP with diabetic CKD G1–G4 and moderately or severely increased albuminuria (A2/A3).
population: Adults with high BP and diabetic CKD.
evidenceNote: Original KDIGO 1B retained; not an ACC/AHA evidence level.
cautions: Assess contraindications and monitoring before prescribing.

title: VA/DoD: diastolic BP goal
summary: At age ≥30 with hypertension, VA/DoD suggests diastolic BP <90 mmHg. Evidence is insufficient to favor <80 over <90.
evidenceNote: Weak for applies to <90; recommendation 6 is neither for nor against <80 versus <90.
cautions: Keep this distinct from ACC/AHA targets; individualize treatment.
